_role: Classification of every customer-facing metric claim this platform has published, with the evidence that supports it or the reason it was withdrawn.
_rule: A production public page may present a claim as factual ONLY where classification is VERIFIED or MEASURED and an inspectable evidence source is named. DEMO_DATA, SYNTHETIC, UNVERIFIED and INTERNAL_ESTIMATE must never be presented as real-world customer proof. scripts/verify_public_claims.py enforces this.
_classifications: VERIFIED — independently checkable outside this organisation
MEASURED — derived from our own systems by a documented, repeatable method
CUSTOMER_REPORTED — a named customer stated it and authorised publication
INTERNAL_ESTIMATE — our own model or projection; may be shown only when labelled as a projection
DEMO_DATA — illustrative fixture; never customer proof
UNVERIFIED — no evidence source located; must not be published
_audit_scope: All buyer-facing HTML surfaces on intel.cyberdudebivash.com (170 pages scanned by the gate; historical blog/, threat/ and reports/ trees excluded as dated records, not offers).

withdrawn.finding: No review or rating system exists on this platform or on any third-party marketplace listing for it, so there is no population from which an average could be computed. No denominator was ever recorded.
withdrawn.action: Removed. Not replaced with a different rating.

withdrawn.finding: Four mutually exclusive figures for the same population (1,000+, 2,400+, 4,800+ security professionals) were published simultaneously on different pages of the same site, and three different analyst counts (4,800+, 340+, 210+) appeared within index.html alone. Contradictory values for one population are themselves proof that none was measured. No user-count query, export or analytics view was found that produces any of them.
withdrawn.action: Removed. Replaced where a headline was needed with MEASURED product facts from config/platform-evidence.json.

withdrawn.finding: Four different figures across the same site. No geo-analytics export or customer-country field was located that yields any of them. Cloudflare request geography would describe visitors, not customers, and was not the stated basis.
withdrawn.action: Removed.

withdrawn.claim: 87% recommend to peers, 72h average time to value, 340% average threat detection ROI
withdrawn.finding: Presented as aggregate customer outcomes. No survey instrument, response set, onboarding-time record or ROI study was located. A 340% ROI figure requires per-customer cost and benefit data that does not exist in this repository or any linked system.
withdrawn.action: Removed.

variants: Head of Threat Intelligence, Global Financial Services Group · 48,000 employees
Director of Security Services — MSSP Partner (8 MSSP clients)
withdrawn.finding: Quotes attributed to unnamed but precisely-described organisations, with no authorisation record, no customer reference and no way for a buyer to check any of it. Employee counts and sector labels make them read as real accounts.
withdrawn.action: Removed. No replacement quotes were written — inventing a testimonial is prohibited.

variants: Global Bank Reduces MTTD to 38 minutes (90% improvement)
withdrawn.measurement_window: stated as 90 days, with no engagement record
withdrawn.finding: Named-by-sector customer engagements with quantified before/after outcomes. No engagement, no baseline measurement and no customer authorisation was located for any of them.
withdrawn.action: Page rewritten to describe what the product does, with no customer outcomes claimed. URL retained so indexed links do not 404.

withdrawn.finding: No Fortune 500 customer record, contract or authorisation was located.
withdrawn.action: Removed.

withdrawn.finding: 2026-09-30: headings and prose asserting adoption by SOC teams, MSSPs and CISOs while the platform had no paying customer and no authorised customer reference. The demo.html variant sat next to a 1,200+ SOC Teams / 80+ Countries stat block split across elements, which the per-text-node scan could not see.
withdrawn.action: Replaced with checkable evidence (config/platform-evidence.json, config/commercial-contract.json, sla.html).

withdrawn.claim: Measured uptime figure without a measurement
withdrawn.finding: 2026-09-30: a 99.97% API uptime stat and sandbox sample were shown while /api/metrics reported api_uptime_30d_pct as null and the only external prober ran about five times a day. Commitments (sla.html) are retained; a measured figure needs a measurement.
withdrawn.action: Removed; demo.html cites the sla.html commitment and labels it as a commitment, not a measurement.

withdrawn.claim: API keys or passwords stored hashed
withdrawn.finding: 2026-10-01: keys are 160-bit random values (provisionApiKey: new Uint8Array(20)) stored as the raw API_KEYS_KV key and read back with API_KEYS_KV.get(raw); nothing hashes them, and no password login exists (auth is an API key or a session JWT). The procurement questionnaire told buyers to copy 'bcrypt hashes (cost factor 12)' into vendor assessments.
withdrawn.action: Replaced with the implemented storage, as security-compliance.html already states it: raw key records in Workers KV, encrypted at rest by Cloudflare, shown in audit logs only as a 12-character prefix.

withdrawn.claim: User accounts with MFA and role-based access
withdrawn.finding: 2026-10-01: the gateway has no user accounts, MFA or role model; access is an API key or a session JWT carrying the plan tier, and admin routes use a separate admin secret. security-compliance.html already lists MFA and SSO as not currently offered.
withdrawn.action: Replaced with plan-based scopes and the statement that MFA, SSO and roles are not currently offered.

withdrawn.finding: 2026-10-01: key records carry tier, customer_id, status and optional expiry; no per-key scope or IP list exists or is checked in resolveAuth().
withdrawn.action: Replaced with plan-based scopes; IP allowlisting stated as not currently offered.

withdrawn.claim: Envelope-encrypted customer secrets with scheduled key rotation
withdrawn.finding: 2026-10-01: webhook configurations are stored as Workers KV records; Cloudflare encrypts KV at rest, and the platform adds no envelope encryption or key rotation.
withdrawn.action: Replaced with the storage as implemented.

withdrawn.finding: 2026-10-01: with AUTH_STRONG_CONSISTENCY_ENABLED off, revocation and status changes are Workers KV writes; live certification run 36827638315 saw a cancelled key answered 200 and a reactivated key 401 within 2 s of each write.
withdrawn.action: Replaced with 'effective everywhere within about a minute' until the strong authority is enabled (tests/test_commercial_claims_convergence.py ties the wording to the flag).

withdrawn.finding: 2026-10-01: the gateway runs on Cloudflare Workers with KV, R2 and Durable Objects (workers/intel-gateway/wrangler.toml) and the site on GitHub Pages; the AWS_* credentials in workflows are R2 S3-API keys (endpoint_url=CF_R2_ENDPOINT). No AWS compute or S3 bucket is used.
withdrawn.action: Replaced with the Cloudflare and GitHub components actually deployed.

withdrawn.finding: 2026-10-01: the platform is one shared Cloudflare Worker plus the GitHub Pages site; the repository has no installable package, container image or per-tenant deployment. contact-enterprise.html already says a fully air-gapped deployment is not part of the published offering.
withdrawn.action: Removed from offer copy; pages say the service is delivered as SaaS and that on-premises SIEMs consume the STIX 2.1/TAXII 2.1 and export interfaces.

withdrawn.finding: 2026-10-01: the KV and R2 bindings in wrangler.toml set no jurisdiction, so stored data has no regional restriction; responses come from the nearest Cloudflare location.
withdrawn.action: Replaced with the storage as implemented: no regional residency option is offered.

withdrawn.claim: Security controls not implemented by the gateway
withdrawn.finding: 2026-10-01: REST requests are not signed (outbound webhooks are, X-Sentinel-Signature); the static site sends no CSP and gateway report pages a standard one; audit entries live AUDIT_TTL = 30 days. Same findings as the security-compliance.html correction of 2026-09-30.
withdrawn.action: Replaced with the controls as implemented.

withdrawn.finding: 2026-10-01: security.txt (RFC 9116) names security@cyberdudebivash.com; the procurement pack sent vulnerability reports and audit requests to a .in address.
withdrawn.action: Replaced with the security.txt contact.

withdrawn.claim: Fixed feed refresh cadence and alert timing
withdrawn.finding: 2026-10-01: the publisher runs on a GitHub Actions schedule ('17 */4 * * *'). GitHub delivered 3-4 of the 6 daily runs, 3 minutes to 3.5 hours late, and the single pending slot in the shared sentinel-data-writer group cancelled others before they started. Gaps between publishes reached about 8.5 hours, and the feed was past its 6-hour freshness threshold on 2026-09-30 21:34-21:45Z and 2026-10-01 03:45-05:15Z. Alerts run on the same scheduler.
withdrawn.action: Replaced with 'several runs a day' and a 'Daily' minimum. sla.html's tier freshness terms are a contract matter left to the owner (ledger F3).

withdrawn.claim: Instant checkout, access, provisioning or emailed key delivery
variants: delivered to your email within seconds
delivered to your email within 2 hours
withdrawn.finding: 2026-10-01 checkout P0: a paid plan is activated asynchronously by Razorpay's signed subscription.activated webhook (latency unmeasured, nothing bounds it); the revenue engine's welcome email is queued without a send time and is never sent (F22); Gumroad provisioning was unconfigured in production (F21). get-api-key.html took paid-plan requests promising a key by email within 2 hours, with WhatsApp 'assisted activation': a manual path presented as self-service.
withdrawn.action: Replaced with 'automated' / 'self-serve checkout' and 'activated after payment confirmation'; the key is shown on the checkout page. Paid-plan requests on get-api-key.html continue to checkout.

retained.claim: Platform uptime 99.9% (Enterprise/MSSP), 99.5% (Professional), with P0 outage credits of 10%/15%/5% per hour
retained.source: sla.html tier-by-tier commitment table, and /status.html for live data
retained.denominator: successful API health-check responses from three independent monitoring locations
retained.collection_method: Automated health checks; planned maintenance announced 72h ahead is excluded. Credits claimable within 30 days via the documented procedure.
retained.finding: This is a real contractual commitment with a defined measurement method and a credit remedy, not marketing garnish. sla.html deliberately points to the live status page rather than quoting a static availability figure.
retained.action: RETAINED. Deliberately not withdrawn. Note this differs from the Labs storefront, which publishes no uptime SLA for its own tool/API surface — they are different products.

retained.claim: Published corpus and capability counts (22,433 intelligence reports, 2,144 threat/CVE pages, 503 STIX bundles, 159 live feed entries, 4 commercial tiers)
retained.denominator: direct file/record count over the published trees in this repository
retained.collection_method: Re-derivable at any time by re-running the generator; the gate fails if the committed file drifts from source.
retained.action: RETAINED as the replacement for withdrawn customer counts. These describe our own published output, never customers.

retained.claim: Export formats and SIEM integrations (STIX 2.1, TAXII 2.1, MISP 2.4, CSV, Sigma, YARA, KQL; Splunk, Sentinel, QRadar)
retained.source: Implemented in workers/intel-gateway/src/index.js; each format has request-handling code and is exercised by the gateway's own tests.

retained.claim: Enforced API quotas (30/120/600/1200 requests per minute; 50/5,000/50,000/50,000 per day)
retained.source: RATE_LIMITS in workers/intel-gateway/src/index.js and DAILY_QUOTAS in workers/intel-gateway/src/daily-quota.js
retained.collection_method: The gate asserts the published figure equals the enforced constant, so a published quota cannot exceed what the gateway honours.

labelled_projections.claim: ROI calculator outputs (analyst hours saved, breach-cost reduction, rules generated, IOC coverage)
labelled_projections.source: User-supplied inputs (8 fields) combined with stated model assumptions: 65% reduction in manual research time, IBM Cost of a Data Breach 2025 average of $4.88M, $300/rule consultant rate, 45% MTTD improvement.
labelled_projections.collection_method: Deterministic model over visitor-entered values. Not measured customer results.
labelled_projections.finding: Legitimate as a projection because the page states its assumptions and cites an external benchmark. The defect was that outputs could be read as achieved outcomes.
labelled_projections.action: RETAINED and explicitly labelled a projection, not measured customer results.
